system_overview: This specification models the Tower of Hanoi puzzle using sequences of integers to represent each tower. The Tower of Hanoi is a mathematical puzzle with three rods and a number of disks of different sizes. All disks start stacked in ascending order of size on one rod (smallest at top). The objective is to move the entire stack to the third rod, moving only one disk at a time and never placing a larger disk on top of a smaller one. The minimum number of moves for n disks is 2^n - 1.
actors_and_components: There are no concurrent actors. The system is a single-player puzzle with exactly three towers (positions) where disks can be placed.
state_variables: The system maintains a tuple of three sequences, one per tower. Each sequence represents a stack of disks on that tower, ordered from top to bottom (the first element is the topmost, smallest disk). Each disk is represented by a natural number indicating its size. The total number of disks across all three towers remains constant throughout execution.
initial_state: The three towers are initialized with configurable starting sequences. The typical configuration places all disks on the first tower in ascending size order (e.g., the sequence 1,2,3 for three disks) with the other two towers empty.
actions: A single move action selects a source tower and a destination tower (which must be different). The move is valid if the source tower is not empty and either the destination tower is empty or the top disk of the source tower is smaller than the top disk of the destination tower. When a move occurs, the top disk is removed from the source tower and placed on top of the destination tower.
safety_properties: Type correctness: the system always has exactly three towers, each being a sequence of natural numbers. Element conservation: the set of disk sizes present across all towers equals the original set of disk sizes. Total count conservation: the total number of disks across all towers remains constant.
liveness_properties: NOT_SPECIFIED. The specification does not assert liveness. The puzzle is solved by checking whether the negation of the solved state is an invariant; a counterexample trace shows the solution. The solved state is when the first two towers are empty and the third tower contains all disks in ascending order.
model_bounds: The initial tower configurations are declared as constants (three sequences). For model checking, typical values are a sequence of 1 through n on the first tower and empty sequences for the other two.
additional_assumptions: Unlike the bitwise variant of this puzzle, this specification represents disks explicitly as integer sizes in sequences, making the ordering constraint straightforward to check. The specification models exactly three towers (not configurable). All legal moves are explored nondeterministically; no solving strategy is imposed.
